opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text: Our operating expenses include general and administrative expenses, including legal, accounting and other expenses related to corporate governance, public reporting and compliance with the various provisions of U.S. securities laws. Increases or decreases in such operating expenses will impact our overall financial performance .

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses primarily relate to organizational costs. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, organizational costs increased due to the recognition of costs incurred prior to the commencement of operations.

da_op.text: FFO, as defined by NAREIT and presented below, is calculated as net income or loss (computed in accordance with GAAP), excluding gains or losses from sales of depreciable real property and impairment write-downs on depreciable real property, plus real estate-related depreciation and amortization.

nonop.text: Changes in our monthly NAV before type-specific items include, without limitation, accruals of our net portfolio income, interest expense, distributions, unrealized/realized gains and losses on assets, any applicable organization and offering costs and any expense reimbursements. Changes in our monthly NAV before type-specific items also include material non-recurring events, such as capital expenditures and material property acquisitions and dispositions occurring during the month. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the Advisor may in its discretion consider material market data and other information that becomes available after the end of the applicable month in valuing our assets and liabilities and calculating our NAV for a particular month. On an ongoing basis, the Advisor will adjust the accruals to reflect actual operating results and the outstanding receivable, payable and other account balances resulting from the accumulation of monthly accruals for which financial information is available.

net.text: We believe funds from operations (“FFO”) is a meaningful supplemental non-GAAP operating metric, which should be considered along with, but not as an alternative to, net income (loss) and cash provided by operating activities as a measure of operating performance. Our consolidated financial statements are presented under historical cost accounting which, among other things, requires depreciation of real estate investments to be calculated on a straight-line basis. As a result, our operating results imply that the value of our real estate investments will decrease evenly over a set time period. net sales.heading: Rental Revenues
net sales.text: We receive income primarily from rental revenue generated by the properties that we acquire. The amount of rental revenue depends upon a number of factors, including our ability to enter into leases with increasing or market value rents for the properties that we acquire and rent collection, which primarily relates to each future tenant’s financial condition and ability to make rent payments to us on time.

intro.text: References herein to “Nuveen Farmland REIT,” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our” refer to Nuveen Farmland REIT, a Maryland statutory trust and its subsidiaries, unless the context specifically requires otherwise. We are a Maryland statutory trust formed on July 21, 2025. We are externally managed by our Advisor, Nuveen Farmland Advisors LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, which is an affiliate of Nuveen.
